correctness.rationale: Every new excitation at the first update is either at the hub (initial hub zero, >=2 initial excited leaves) or at a peripheral leaf (initial hub and its partner both one). The exclusive alternatives force zero new excitations at the second update, with no state ones thereafter. The initial colour countdown and two disjoint first-update triggering events give an exact partition into extinction-time strata for all integers k>=3,m>=1; sum equals k^(2m+1), and the k layer is positive for m=1. Fourteen complete microscopic state-space enumerations agreed with all formulas and exact cutoffs; finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

evidence: Published densest-subgraph theorem 352367f51e91, RESULT.md, proves 3-state extinction when maximum induced edges-per-vertex rho<q and gives a non-sharp excitation budget.

On W_m the maximum induced density is <2: every nonempty petal subgraph has at most 3m edges on 2m+1 vertices, and arbitrary induced subsets cannot exceed 3/2 edges per vertex; hence the general theorem covers eventual extinction for k=3.
Published wheel theorem 58917bc0decb proves threshold-two, three-state extinction by step 5 with sharp wheel size classes, not this arbitrary-k census.

The density proof only uses the fact that successive excitations at one site are at least three time steps apart; this remains valid for every k>=3, so its qualitative extinction mechanism extends to longer refractory chains.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The weaker statement all configurations eventually extinguish at k=3 is covered, and the published argument extends to k>=3; eventual extinction at any k is explicitly excluded from novelty. A generic upper bound depending on the initial excitation count does not determine the exact k-step cutoff or the N_0,...,N_k populations; its theorem applies only to three states and does not imply the arbitrary-k limit law. Wheel graphs and friendship graphs differ even in their rim edges and their exact sharp time.

originality.rationale: Comparisons of the exact statement, not titles alone, found no published all-k, all-m two-contact labelled extinction-time polynomial for friendship graphs. The general induced-density theorem already implies the weaker 3-state eventual-extinction conclusion, which is not claimed as novel. The published threshold-one friendship graphs admit three-cycles and have distinct ten-class censuses; the published three-state two-contact wheel theorem addresses a different family and gives no friendship-graph all-k histogram. Fretter et al. use relative thresholds and single-seed network experiments. Historical unindexed equivalents remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical windmill threshold-two exact all-colour basin formulas could exist.
Full 1993 Durrett–Griffeath preprint and 1978 Greenberg–Hastings original paper were not materially readable here; their abstracts alone are not used to claim full-document noncoverage.
The general density criterion covers eventual extinction for three states, so the main claim must remain the exact multi-colour hitting-time distribution and sharp clock.

value.rationale: The natural friendship-graph family has an unbounded hub and exactly paired peripheral interactions; at the critical contact threshold two it exhibits a nontrivial one-generation causal truncation, in sharp contrast to published period-three behavior at contact threshold one. The contribution quantifies every initial state across two unbounded parameters, yields a sharp all-k extinction clock and an asymptotic two-layer 2/k versus 1-2/k law. These exact transient facts are not a routine restatement of the previously known qualitative density-based extinction criterion, whose proof extends to all k>=3.
